reviews.title: AS3 mathematics and object foundation in an ordinary inventory export
reviews.reason: Bounded coordinator acceptance of the existing typed-collections ordinary export: numeric Class aliases and bound numeric methods, public source-object properties/reflection and Array insertion/removal. Shared-delivery and affected-replay evidence retains the timing boundaries below; visible inventory commands/Restart are accepted only for the unchanged AS3 feature paths of the captured source snapshot; later unrelated source edits are excluded. Final snapshot captured after the shared run collected all 24 project families (23 passed; typed-collections required a fixture LF/CR expectation correction) and after the numeric fixtures passed following restoration of native toString/valueOf behavior. Affected typed-family replay and final browser observations are recorded separately. This is not a fresh all-family run on the final snapshot. Bounded AS3 foundation scenario accepted. The original shared run collected all 24 project workflows: 23 passed and typed-collections failed only its fixture LF-versus-TextField-CR expectation. The focused typed-collections replay passed after correcting that expectation. Numeric fixture replay passed after preserving previous native toString/valueOf semantics. Browser observations before that numeric change covered initial quantity 13/sqrt 3.61 and two actions 16/4.00 and 17/4.12, with object/reflection flags true. A fresh export after the numeric change passed initial state, first action and Restart back to 13/3.61. No full all-family rerun on the final snapshot or original Flash differential execution is claimed. The review retains the 19:15:55 UTC source fingerprints. Subsequent concurrent AS1/SWF6 case-name routing and button-state additions in shared compiler/containers/runtime/web registration files are excluded. The AS3-owned implementation and test files were confirmed unchanged. Later export/Restart observations do not independently accept those unrelated additions, and currentSourceVerified remains false.
reviews.limitations: Bounded coordinator evidence only. Ordinary AS3 source classes and plain records, with explicit unsupported reflection diagnostics; no full native/AS2/bytecode/ApplicationDomain/prototype/AVM2 conformance. Existing partial decisions stay partial. Original Flash differential execution is not claimed. Browser observation and automated real-WASM execution must be recorded separately. The recorded HEAD does not by itself identify the working-tree bytes. The review retains the 19:15:55 UTC source fingerprints. Subsequent concurrent AS1/SWF6 case-name routing and button-state additions in shared compiler/containers/runtime/web registration files are excluded. The AS3-owned implementation and test files were confirmed unchanged. Later export/Restart observations do not independently accept those unrelated additions, and currentSourceVerified remains false.

reviewedEntries.scopeNote: First-class int Class value assigned to a local Class-typed variable and used for numeric construction; exact MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE reads. No complete class/prototype/AVM2 type identity claim.
First-class uint Class value assigned to a local Class-typed variable and used for wrapping construction; exact MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE reads. No complete class/prototype/AVM2 type identity claim.
Ordinary exported AS3 project uses new through an int Class alias on the finite numeric string 42.9 and observes 42. Other conversion and initialization paths retain their existing limits.
Ordinary exported AS3 project uses new through a uint Class alias on -1 and observes 4294967295. General coercion and all boundary/error paths are not inferred from this representative check.
The AS3 int class exposes MIN_VALUE as -2147483648 in the combined ordinary-export inventory scenario.
The AS3 int class exposes MAX_VALUE as 2147483647 in the combined ordinary-export inventory scenario.
The AS3 uint class exposes MIN_VALUE as 0 in the combined ordinary-export inventory scenario.
The AS3 uint class exposes MAX_VALUE as 4294967295 in the combined ordinary-export inventory scenario.

Existing shared Rust-backed sqrt is extracted as a Function and called on changing inventory totals 13, 16 and 17; this refreshes bounded integration evidence rather than claiming a new complete Math implementation.

Number.toFixed extracted from sqrt(total) retains its numeric receiver for direct calls, call with another receiver and apply(null,[2]); observed results 3.61, 4.00 and 4.12. This does not certify all rounding/exponent/range/coercion cases.

Plain record hidden dynamic property remains owned and readable; an ordinary AS3 source-class public quantity slot is reported as own. Native display/AS2/hidden trait and general AVM2 object conformance are outside this scenario.

Plain record dynamic metadata marked hidden reports false; ordinary AS3 source-class fixed public quantity slot also remains nonenumerable. The visible record properties remain the for-in keys count and quantity.
Hiding an existing own configurable dynamic metadata property removes it from for-in without deleting ownership, membership or its readable value. Fixed/native/AS2 traits are not made dynamic.
An ordinary source-class app.Item instance reports app::Item during the published inventory workflow. This does not infer complete primitive/native/bytecode type identity.
An ordinary source-class app.Item instance rooted in Object reports Object during the published inventory workflow; arbitrary native-base hierarchies are outside this evidence.

Public registered app.Item source class resolves by both app.Item and app::Item and retains equality with its class value. Arbitrary loaded bytecode, ApplicationDomain and hidden definitions are not supported by this scope.

Ordinary source-class app.Item instance produces XML with public quantity:int variable and stockLabel accessor metadata without invoking that getter. Native-base, interface and unsupported rest-parameter descriptions retain explicit diagnostics; no complete AVM2 reflection claim.
An ordinary AS3 Array inserts the newest batch at index 0 in place, preserving the recent-history array across actions. This Player 19 API is not attributed to earlier Player versions.

An ordinary AS3 Array removes and returns its last entry using index -1, preserving the newest two batches across repeated actions and reset. General sparse/large-index/coercion cases need their own existing evidence.
